in_kind_convention: monetary-only closed exactly on BOTH sides (7,690.00 and 6,611.19). Both conventions tested and numerically identical here: the filer's own ledgers have no in-kind column and mark no row in kind, and the county summary page prints no separate in-kind line.
escalation_note: Eight 900 dpi tight-cell crops, all for GEOMETRY PROOF - none was needed to settle a figure, because pages 3-5 are TYPED at high contrast and every amount is unambiguous at full-page resolution. The crops proved the first and last transcribed band of each of the three ledger pages plus two one-past-the-end negative controls; what each rendered is recorded in the frames' measure_notes.

3.measure_note: ⚠ THIS IS NOT THE COUNTY'S UNDERLINE FORM. Pages 3-5 are the candidate's OWN TYPED SPREADSHEET ledger (§A2 pattern), a fully BOXED grid, so a row lies BETWEEN ITS OWN RULES and the text-above-the-rule convention does NOT apply here - nothing is extrapolated. rowbands.py on the RAW frame (deskew 0.0 deg) returns 21 horizontal rules 6.66 .. 46.64 pct at a regular ~2.0 pct pitch and 4 vertical rules 6.36 / 16.15 / 26.52 / 50.76, which are the table's left edge and its three column dividers: Date 6.36-16.15, AMOUNT 16.15-26.52, Donor 26.52-50.76. The 20 stored bands are the full printed grid: band 1 is the ledger's own 'Schedule A | Contributions' caption row, band 2 is its 'Date | Amount | Donor' header, bands 3-14 are the TWELVE data rows, bands 15-17 are blank, band 18 is its 'Total $7,690' row and bands 19-20 are blank. Row indices in this record are these printed band numbers, so line 1 sits at row 3. PROOF at 900 dpi with --value: the first transcribed band, pct:16.15,10.64,10.37,2.00@p3, rendered '$2,000' (recorded 2000); the last, pct:16.15,32.64,10.37,2.00@p3, rendered '$400' (recorded 400); and the §B5 one-past-the-end control pct:16.15,34.64,10.37,1.97@p3 rendered an EMPTY boxed cell.

4.measure_note: Same typed BOXED ledger, measured separately on its own page. rowbands.py returns 43 rules 6.66 .. 90.82 pct (~2.0 pct pitch, deskew 0.0) and vertical rules 6.42 / 16.06 / 24.94 / 53.49 giving Date 6.42-16.06, AMOUNT 16.06-24.94, Payable 24.94-53.49. The 42 stored bands are the whole printed grid: band 1 is the 'Schedule B | Expenditures' caption, band 2 the 'Date | Amount | Payable' header, and bands 3-42 are the FORTY data rows, so expenditure line 1 sits at row 3 and line 40 at row 42. PROOF at 900 dpi with --value: first transcribed band pct:16.06,10.66,8.88,2.09@p4 rendered '$60.81' (recorded 60.81); last transcribed band pct:16.06,88.84,8.88,1.98@p4 rendered '$46.00' (recorded 46.00). There is no band 43 to use as a negative control - the printed grid ENDS at rule 90.82 and the ledger continues on p5, whose band 1 was itself proved by crop; the p5 negative control stands for the tail of the side.

5.measure_note: The CONTINUATION sheet of the same typed boxed ledger - it carries NO caption and NO header row, so band 1 is a DATA row here while on pages 3 and 4 band 1 is a caption. That is exactly why each page was measured on its own and no grid was carried across. rowbands.py returns 15 rules 6.70 .. 36.73 pct (deskew 0.0) and vertical rules 6.33 / 15.97 / 24.82 / 53.40 giving Date 6.33-15.97, AMOUNT 15.97-24.82, Payable 24.82-53.40. Bands 1-5 are the five data rows, band 6 is blank, band 7 is the ledger's own total row '$6,611.19'. ⚠ ONE FAINT RULE AT ~22.7 PCT WAS NOT DETECTED, so stored band 8 [20.75, 24.70] is a DOUBLE band spanning two printed rows; it lies below every transcribed row and below the total row, so no row index in this record is affected - recorded here rather than silently patched. PROOF at 900 dpi with --value: first transcribed band pct:15.97,6.70,8.85,2.03@p5 rendered '$150.00' (recorded 150.00); last transcribed band pct:15.97,14.68,8.85,2.05@p5 rendered '$705.09' (recorded 705.09); the §B5 one-past-the-end control pct:15.97,16.73,8.85,1.97@p5 rendered an EMPTY boxed cell.

Page-face office 'County Commission Seat B', which agrees with the channel. Report type ticked '30 Days after withdraw or elimination'; amendment ticked 'No'; party 'Republican'; date '6 May 2014' (day-month-year in words, the same unusual form Guernsey uses in this chunk). FIVE pages, each classified from its own printed heading: p1 the 2014 cover (Utah County Code 2-5), p2 'SUMMARY PAGE', p3 the filer's OWN TYPED LEDGER captioned 'Schedule A | Contributions', p4 the same ledger captioned 'Schedule B | Expenditures', p5 its unheaded CONTINUATION sheet. ⚠ THE COUNTY'S SCHEDULE A AND SCHEDULE B FORMS ARE NOT USED AT ALL - the sides are still 'transcribed' because what is missing is the county's FORM, not the filer's entries (the §A2 precedent, and this is a second, cleaner instance of it: a portrait boxed spreadsheet rather than a skewed landscape one). Consequences worth carrying: the ledger has columns Date / Amount / Donor|Payable and NO ADDRESS COLUMN AND NO PURPOSE COLUMN, so every donor city/state and every purpose on this filing is blank BECAUSE THE DOCUMENT HAS NO SUCH FIELD - a distinct cause from redacted-by-the-county, left-empty-by-the-filer, form-prints-a-zip-and-no-city, and lost-in-reproduction, and the fifth such cause now on record. Both sides close exactly on the promoted per-period Column A cell and on the filer's own printed ledger totals. Summary line 3 (Balance at Beginning) is an EMPTY CELL - not a zero glyph, not a dash - and was left blank. Four of the 45 expenditure rows and one of the 12 contribution rows are dated in DECEMBER 2013, before the cycle year: well-formed, early, kept verbatim.
